cohort: The study participants were preterm infants whose oxygen saturation (SpO2) was continuously monitored using high-resolution pulse oximeters during the first 10 weeks of life.
finding: For most analyses, there was no significant association between intermittent hypoxemia (IH) and Type 1 ROP after adjusting for gestational age (GA) and birth weight (BW), except for cumulative IH of longer duration during the second month of life (weeks 5-10, 6-10, and 7-10), which was associated with a higher risk for Type 1 ROP.
